task_s.task_description: Analyze the queried data to identify patterns and correlations between sleep quality, premature heartbeats, and lifestyle factors. Determine the root causes of poor sleep and premature heartbeats.
task_s.response:
1、Sleep quality is strongly correlated with sleep onset time: earlier bedtimes (before 11 PM) were associated with longer sleep duration and higher sleep scores, while late bedtimes (after midnight) led to short sleep and poor quality.
2、Premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) tend to occur more frequently on days with poor sleep quality. Days following low sleep scores (≤65) averaged 1.75 PVCs, compared to 0.5 PVCs after good sleep (score ≥75).
3、Exercise, particularly morning activity, was linked to improved sleep and lower PVC occurrence. On exercise days (Mar 25 and 28), sleep scores were high (80, 85) and PVC counts were low (0 and 1).
4、Daily steps and calorie expenditure did not show a direct correlation with sleep quality; high activity alone did not prevent poor sleep if sleep onset was late.
5、Sedentary periods were reduced on days with higher steps but did not independently predict sleep or PVCs.
6、The root cause of poor sleep appears to be irregular sleep timing, specifically late-night bedtimes, possibly due to lifestyle or work demands not captured. This irregular schedule may also contribute to cardiac irritability, as indicated by PVCs.

task_s.task_description: Based on the analysis, provide actionable advice to improve sleep and reduce premature heartbeats. Point out any unhealthy lifestyle habits and suggest improvements.

3、Avoid late-night activities that delay sleep onset, even on days with high physical activity, since late bedtimes negate the benefits of exercise on sleep.
4、Establish a regular sleep schedule to reduce cardiac irritability and the occurrence of premature ventricular contractions.
